cells.tense: Something is arriving right now, and you are here to meet it.
cells.verb: letting what you feel and what you can picture join into one current
cells.place: at the threshold where something new is just coming in
cells.ask: Let that joining pick a direction, and hold the direction when something leans against it — not harder than it needs, just steadily enough that the choice stays yours. What comes back is a sense of where you're going that you don't have to argue yourself into.
cells.core:
Something is arriving right now, and you are here to meet it. You can feel it and you can see where it might go, and the two aren't fighting — they're moving together, and the moving is a choice you're making, not something happening to you. That is rarer than it sounds: most people either feel a thing or picture it, and you're doing both in one motion.

What this is free to feed next is a direction. Let the joining pick one, and hold it when something leans against it — not harder than it needs, just steadily enough that the choice stays yours. What comes back is a sense of where you're going that you don't have to argue yourself into.
cells.sheetLine: You're meeting what's arriving with feeling and sight together, by choice.

cells.tense: You're already living in the version where this has become everything.
cells.verb: fusing with what's arriving before it has finished arriving
cells.place: at the threshold where something new is just coming in
cells.ask: Tend what's arriving without closing your hand on it — give it room and time the way you'd give a planted thing room, and let it show you what it's becoming at its own pace. What comes back is a picture of where this goes that grows out of what actually happened, not out of what you needed it to be.
cells.core:
You're already living in the version where this has become everything. It's barely through the door and you've decided what it is, where it goes, how it ends — you've poured yourself into it before it had a chance to be itself. The deciding is running ahead of the arriving, and it's the arriving that was supposed to tell you what to decide.

Try tending what's arriving without closing your hand on it. Give it room and time the way you'd give a planted thing room, and let it show you what it's becoming at its own pace. What comes back is a picture of where this goes that grows out of what actually happened, not out of what you needed it to be.
cells.sheetLine: You've decided what this is before it finished arriving.

cells.tense: Something has already come through the door, and you're still standing where it was before it came.
cells.verb: holding back from the joining you can feel the shape of
cells.place: at the threshold where something new is just coming in
cells.ask: Rather than trying to feel your way in, name what you actually perceive about this — all of it, even the parts that don't agree, even the part that says you don't know yet — and let the knowing be accurate before you ask it to be warm. What comes back is a sense of this that's whole enough to want, because you've taken in what it actually is.
cells.core:
Something has already come through the door, and you're still standing where it was before it came. You can feel the shape of a joining and you're not stepping into it — not refusing, exactly, just not arriving. The feeling is there in outline. The choice to let it meet you hasn't been made, and the moment it was easiest to make is a little behind you now.

Rather than trying to feel your way in, name what you actually perceive about this — all of it, even the parts that don't agree, even the part that says you don't know yet — and let the knowing be accurate before you ask it to be warm. What comes back is a sense of this that's whole enough to want, because you've taken in what it actually is.
cells.sheetLine: It's arrived. You haven't let yourself meet it yet.

cells.tense: You've already joined with this — the pen is in your hand and you're calling it the weather.
cells.verb: choosing a connection and describing it as something that just happened
cells.place: at the threshold where something new is just coming in
cells.ask: Lay out, plainly, for one person, the path you're already on with this — step by step, as if they might need to walk it — and notice who is doing the steering as you describe it. What comes back is a picture of where this goes that you can stand inside, because you've admitted you're the one drawing it.
cells.core:
You've already joined with this — the pen is in your hand and you're calling it the weather. What's arriving has met you and you've met it back, decisively, and the current is moving with you in it. But when you talk about it you say it found you, it swept you up, it was just timing. The choosing happened. The owning of the choice is what hasn't.

Lay out, plainly, for one person, the path you're already on with this — step by step, as if they might need to walk it — and notice who is doing the steering as you describe it. What comes back is a picture of where this goes that you can stand inside, because you've admitted you're the one drawing it.
cells.sheetLine: You already chose this. You're still calling it something that happened to you.
